transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because the routing system at the warehouse isn’t just a computer anymore. It’s been marking my moves and sending messages through the scanners, trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands.
Have you been using any drugs or alcohol recently, or have you used them regularly in the past?
I’m not sure what you mean by regularly. I haven’t really been keeping track of that.
How long have you been noticing these messages and feeling that the system is targeting you—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been a while—about a year and eight months, I’d say. The scanners started sending the messages around then, and it hasn’t let up.
During this time, have you had periods where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal?
No, I can’t say I’ve had times like that. I haven’t noticed feeling unusually energetic or needing less sleep.
Can you tell me whether you have used any alcohol, marijuana, stimulants, or other drugs in the past month, and if so, how often and how much?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t been keeping track of what I use or how often.
In the past month, have you used any alcohol, marijuana, or other drugs at all, even just once?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really kept track of whether I used anything this past month.
During this past year and eight months, have you had any stretches where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
Yeah. Things I used to enjoy just don’t pull me in anymore. Fishing, choir practice, working with wood in my garage—I can look right at my rods or my tools and feel no interest in touching them.
How long have you been feeling this way—uninterested in fishing, choir, and woodworking—compared to when the messages from the scanners started?
It’s been going on for a while. The fishing, choir, and working with wood used to settle me, but now I can stand there looking at my rods or my tools and just feel no pull to do any of it.
Since the messages from the scanners started about a year and eight months ago, have you been using alcohol, marijuana, or any other substances on a regular basis during that time?
I honestly can’t say for sure. I haven’t kept track of whether I was using anything regularly during that time.

Has there been a time during this year and eight months when you felt the scanners were sending you messages, but you did NOT feel sad or uninterested in things—that is, did the psychotic experiences ever occur without the depression?

Yeah. There was a stretch where my mood had eased up some—I was eating and talking a little more—but for several weeks I still heard dispatch calling my number and felt like the routing system was tracking me.
That stretch when your mood eased up but you still heard the dispatch messages—about how many weeks or months did that period last?
I’d say several weeks, not months. My mood was a little better then, but the dispatch messages and feeling tracked were still there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent psychotic syndrome (delusions of being tracked/targeted via warehouse scanners, auditory hallucinations of 'dispatch calling his number') lasting approximately 20 months. For most of this period, he also met criteria for a major depressive episode (anhedonia across multiple domains—fishing, choir, woodworking). Critically, he described a several-week period during which mood symptoms improved (better mood, eating, talking) but psychotic symptoms (delusions, hallucinations) persisted, satisfying the criterion that psychotic symptoms occur for a substantial period in the absence of a mood episode. No manic or hypomanic symptoms were ever endorsed, ruling out the bipolar subtype (F25.0). Substance use could not be clearly excluded but was not confirmed as a better explanation. The combination of concurrent mood (depressive-only) and psychotic symptoms, plus psychosis outlasting the mood episode, is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type (F25.1) rather than Bipolar Type (F25.0), Schizophrenia (F20.9), or Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features (F32.3), the latter being excluded because psychotic symptoms persisted beyond the resolution of mood symptoms.
